core_obligations: Translate the subset (proof lines 1088-1091): let Z be the inverse image of the closed subset T of the space of connected components; then Z is the intersection of the open and closed subsets Z_alpha of X containing it.
Describe the pieces (proof lines 1091-1093): each Z_alpha is the spectrum of an algebra A_alpha over A obtained by localizing at an idempotent, so A -> A_alpha is a local isomorphism.
Take the colimit (proof lines 1093-1094): setting B equal to the colimit of the A_alpha makes A -> B a surjective ind-Zariski map whose spectrum is homeomorphic to Z, as required.
proof_roadmap: Write the inverse image of the closed subset as an intersection of open and closed pieces.
Identify each piece as the spectrum of a localization at an idempotent.
Take the colimit of the resulting system.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that for a ring A and a closed subset T of the space of connected components of its spectrum there is a surjective ind-Zariski map A -> B inducing a homeomorphism of Spec(B) with the inverse image of T (statement lines 1080-1086). The proof (proof lines 1088-1095) writes that inverse image as an intersection of open and closed subsets, identifies each with the spectrum of a localization at an idempotent, and takes the colimit. H2: a three-step explicit construction with two inputs, written out in full.
